title: Nancy Guthrie Ransom Note Excerpts Revealed on Crime Junkie Podcast
excerpt: A journalist read aloud from the first ransom note in the Savannah Guthrie mother kidnapping case, revealing demands for millions in Bitcoin and a chilling warning that Nancy's 'life is in your hands.'
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Nancy Guthrie was kidnapped, with ransom demands revealed on the Crime Junkie podcast.
  • The first ransom note demanded $4 million in Bitcoin by February 5.
  • A second note claimed Nancy had died, while a third offered video evidence for money.
  • The FBI is investigating the authenticity of the ransom notes.
  • Savannah Guthrie pleads for information, with a reward exceeding $1.2 million.

New excerpts from the first ransom note in the Nancy Guthrie kidnapping case were revealed Wednesday on the Crime Junkie podcast, offering the most detailed public account yet of the demands made after the 84-year-old was taken from her Tucson, Arizona, home nearly six months ago.

Crime journalist Briana Whitney, who covered the case for Phoenix-based AZ Family, joined Crime Junkie host Ashley Flowers to read portions of the note aloud. A spokesperson for the podcast said the hosts would not release copies of the text, which has not been independently verified.

What the First Note Said

The note was addressed directly to Nancy's daughter, Today show co-anchor Savannah Guthrie.

"Hello, Savannah. We have your mother, Nancy. She is safe but scared. She will be held for ransom, and once payment is received, she will be released unharmed. We will be holding her for a maximum of seven days."

— Excerpt from the first ransom note, read by Briana Whitney

The sender demanded payment in Bitcoin, setting two escalating deadlines: $4 million by Thursday, February 5, and $6 million by Monday, February 9 at 5 p.m., according to People, citing sources familiar with the note.

Whitney continued reading: "Once payment is received to the Bitcoin address below, she will be released within 12 hours of deposit to a safe drop-off location back in Tucson. If the payment is not received by the last deadline on Monday the 9th at 5 p.m., she will be killed. Your mother is aware of this and her life is in your hands."

The note left no room for negotiation. "You will not be able to contact me from here on out. There will be no negotiation. Do not play games. Law enforcement will not be able to help you," Whitney read.

Crime Scene Details in the Note

The sender also included specific details about Nancy's home that may have only been known to investigators and the suspect at the time. Whitney said the note referenced a white smartwatch found on the floor near Guthrie's bed and a floodlight in the backyard that had been destroyed — information that would not have been public knowledge when the note was sent.

The FBI is still investigating whether the note is genuine. A second note, sent after the first deadline passed, claimed Nancy had died shortly after being taken. That note did not include an apology or a demand for further payment, according to NBC News. A third note, sent to TMZ and forwarded to the FBI on June 26, offered to sell a video and identifying information about the suspects in exchange for money.

![Ashley Flowers. Crime journalist Briana Whitney, who covered the case for Phoenix-based AZ Family, joined Crime Junkie host Ashley Flowers to read portions of the note aloud.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7c/Ashley_Flowers.jpg)

Which Notes Are Real?

At least three ransom notes have been received since Nancy's disappearance. Earlier this month, reports suggested none were believed genuine. The FBI later clarified that only some had been dismissed as fakes.

"This case continues to be investigated as a kidnapping for ransom case. The FBI has and will continue to offer all assistance possible in the investigation — however local authorities remain the lead."

— FBI National Press Office

The only known suspect remains publicly unidentified — a masked intruder captured on Nest doorbell camera footage that the FBI recovered with assistance from Google. He is described as between 5 feet 9 inches and 5 feet 10 inches tall with an average build, wearing a black Ozark Trail backpack.

Savannah Guthrie's Plea

Savannah, 54, returned to her role as Today co-anchor on April 6 after a two-month absence. She has been publicly vocal about her anguish.

"I cry every morning on the way to work, and I cry every morning on the way home," she said on Today with Jenna & Sheinelle in June. "We can hold our sadness and we can hold our joy. And if you don't believe it, just watch me."

In a statement to KOLD, Savannah reflected on "five months of agony and unending trauma" and urged people with information to come forward. "There is not a moment that goes by that we aren't actively trying to find our mom," she said.

The combined reward for information in the case now exceeds $1.2 million. Anyone with tips is asked to call 1-800-CALL-FBI or submit information anonymously through Tucson's Crime Stoppers at 520-88-CRIME.
